_about.what: Pieces many moves share, referred to by name from the moves files. Add here when the same measurement, fault or pose would otherwise be typed twice.
_about.measurements: name → { "kind", "pts", "per", "sign", "abs", "flip" }. kinds: "angle" (3 points: the angle at the middle one, 0–180°), "vertical" (2: the segment's angle from hanging straight down, 90 = horizontal), "tilt" (2: from horizontal, 90 = upright), "dist" (2: distance, % of the reference length), "offset" (3: how far the third sits off the line through the first two, % of that line, + = below), "rise" (1: how far the point has risen since calibration, %), "height" (2: how far the first point is above the second, %), "ratio" (2: the segment's length vs calibration, 100 = unchanged — a limb leaving the camera plane reads shorter), "gap" (2: sideways offset of the first point from the second, %; "sign": "outward" = away from the midline, "forward" = the way the toes point), "rotation" (2: how far a segment has swung toward the camera, degrees), "near" (3: distance from the first point to the segment between the others, %), "lean" (0: trunk lean, + = toward the working side, or the way the toes point with "sign": "forward"), "headTilt" (0: head roll against the pelvis), "pelvis" (0: pelvis tilt seen from the front). "per" = what a % is of: "torso" (default), a segment ["KNEE", "ANK"], or "height" — the person's standing height, estimated from their own trunk, thigh and shin at calibration, so a knee that drifts 5 % of height reads the same on a tall person and a short one. With "per": "height" the reading may also be given in real length: "unit": "in" or "cm" turns that share of height into inches or centimetres using the height the person set in the app (5'11" unless they changed it), and every threshold on the measurement is then written in that unit. Good: a knee-over-toe gap of 2 in. Bad: inches on a % of torso (nothing else on the body has a known length). "abs": true ignores the sign. "flip": { "option": "variant", "when": "ir" } negates the reading for that option value. Point names: NOSE EAR SH EL WR HIP KNEE ANK HEEL FOOT on the working side; put o in front for the other side (oKNEE); mEAR mSH mHIP for midpoints.
_about.faults: name → a complete fault. A move writes { "template": "lean", "threshold": 60 } and gets this fault with that threshold; any field the move writes wins over the template's. A template without a threshold requires the move to give one. Foot on the floor: heel_up, toes_up and foot_up watch the heel, the toes or the whole foot (ankle) rising since calibration, as a % of shin length (10 ≈ a few centimetres); the person's start position is where the floor is, so the phone only needs to see the foot. Add "phase": "any" on a hold, "minP" to ignore the start of a rep, or "pts": ["oHEEL"] via your own measurement for the other foot.
_about.poses: name → keyframe angles. A move writes { "preset": "standing", "uarm": 20 } and gets these values with its own on top.
_about.holds: name → a list of hold conditions, used by hold moves as "conditions": "balance".

lean.label: Leaning the trunk
lean.tip: The trunk tipping forward shifts the work to the back and hips. Chest up, look ahead.

fold.label: Trunk folding forward
fold.tip: A little forward lean is normal; folding shifts the load to the lower back.

valgus.label: Knees caving inward
valgus.tip: Screw the feet into the floor and push the knees over the little toes.

kneebend.label: Knees bending too much
kneebend.tip: The knees stay softly bent while the hips travel back; bending them turns it into a squat.

shrug.label: Shrugging the shoulder up
shrug.tip: The shoulder blade should glide, not hike toward the ear. Lower the shoulder before the arm rises.

shrug_lift.label: Shoulders shrugging up
shrug_lift.tip: If the shoulders rise toward the ears, the upper trapezius has taken over. Lower the weight.

swing.label: Upper arm swinging
swing.tip: The upper arm hangs still; only the forearm moves. Swinging is momentum, not muscle.

heel_up.label: Heel lifting
heel_up.tip: The heel came off the floor. Sit back into the hips and keep the weight through the whole foot; raise the heels on a small plate if they will not stay down.

toes_up.label: Toes lifting
toes_up.tip: The front of the foot came off the floor — the weight has gone back into the heels. Spread the toes and press the ball of the foot down.

foot_up.label: Foot leaving the floor
foot_up.tip: The foot lifted off the floor. It should stay planted for the whole rep.
